title: Tokyo to Kyoto: Neon, Temples & Private Onsen: 11 days across Japan — from teamLab's digital cosmos to Nintendo's playground, Himeji's white heron castle, a private Hakone onsen, and two nights at the Park Hyatt's Lost in Translation bar
description: A multi-city journey through the beating heart of Japan. Start in electric Tokyo with teamLab Borderless and Golden Gai. Bullet train to Kyoto for Fushimi Inari, the Nintendo Museum, and a chopstick making class. Day trip to Himeji Castle. Eat your way through Osaka. Escape to Hakone for a private onsen night in the mountains. Return to Tokyo in style at the Park Hyatt, where Lost in Translation's New York Bar awaits on the 52nd floor. Every special request woven in, every meal researched, every minute considered.

days.title: Arrival & First Taste of Tokyo
days.description: Touch down at NRT, clear customs, and ease into Tokyo with an evening in electric Shinjuku. No rushing — you just flew across the world.

activities.time: ✈️ 4:30 PM — Land at Narita International Airport
activities.name: Immigration & Customs
activities.description: Expect 45–90 minutes for immigration, baggage claim, and customs. Visit Japan Web (pre-register online) speeds things up significantly. Have your QR code ready on your phone.

activities.name: N'EX (Narita Express) to Shinjuku Station
activities.description: The most comfortable option into central Tokyo. Reserved seats, luggage racks, about 80 minutes direct to Shinjuku. Buy tickets at the JR ticket counter in the airport basement.

activities.name: Omoide Yokochō (Memory Lane / Piss Alley)
activities.description: Narrow alleyways packed with tiny yakitori and ramen joints, each seating maybe 6–8 people. Smoky, loud, and absolutely iconic. This is the Tokyo welcome you want.

activities.name: Kabukichō Nightlife District
activities.description: A quick stroll through Tokyo's most famous entertainment district. Neon signs stacked ten stories high, host clubs, arcades, and the famous Godzilla head on the Toho Building. Great for photos even if you don't go in anywhere.

days.title: teamLab Borderless, Tsukiji & Shibuya Nights
days.description: Immerse yourself in digital art at teamLab Borderless, graze through Tsukiji's outer market, then experience Shibuya crossing and Tokyo's best cocktail bars.

activities.time: 🌅 9:00 AM — teamLab Borderless at Azabudai Hills
activities.name: teamLab Borderless: MORI Building Digital Art Museum
activities.description: The world's first museum of borderless digital art, reopened at Azabudai Hills in 2024. Artworks flow from room to room with no boundaries — you wander freely through immersive light installations that react to your presence. Plan 2–3 hours minimum.

activities.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Street Food Crawl
activities.description: The inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market is still the best food crawl in Tokyo. Hundreds of stalls selling fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki (sweet egg), grilled scallops, strawberry daifuku, and more.

activities.name: Shibuya Crossing & Surrounding Area
activities.description: The world's busiest pedestrian crossing. Watch from the Starbucks above (2F of Tsutaya Building) for the overhead view, then walk across yourself. Explore the streets around Shibuya for shopping, record stores, and people-watching.

activities.name: Afuri Ramen (Ebisu Location)
activities.description: Light, citrusy yuzu shio ramen that's a perfect counterpoint to heavy tonkotsu. The original Ebisu location is a local favorite — small, no-frills, and absolutely delicious.

activities.name: Bar Hopping in Shibuya
activities.description: Shibuya has some of Tokyo's best bars. Try a whisky bar, a standing bar (tachinomi), or a themed izakaya.

days.title: Asakusa, Akihabara & Golden Gai
days.description: Old-world Tokyo meets otaku culture. Morning at Sensō-ji temple, afternoon in electric Akihabara, evening in the legendary Golden Gai tiny bars.

activities.name: Sensō-ji Temple
activities.description: Tokyo's oldest and most visited temple. The massive Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) with its giant red lantern is iconic. Walk through Nakamise-dōri shopping street to reach the main hall. Arrive early to beat the crowds.

activities.name: Asakusa Morning Food & Culture
activities.description: Grab melon pan from Kagetsudo (the Instagram-famous giant melon pan), then explore the backstreets of Asakusa. The area around Kappabashi-dōri (Kitchen Town) has incredible knife shops and plastic food replicas.

activities.name: Akihabara Electric Town
activities.description: Japan's otaku mecca. Multi-story arcades, retro game shops, anime merch, and maid cafés. Even if you're not into anime, the sheer density of neon and energy is an experience.

activities.name: Ueno Park & Museums
activities.description: If you want a culture break from Akihabara, Ueno Park is a 10-min walk away. Home to Tokyo National Museum (Japan's largest), the stunning Shinobazu Pond, and several shrines.

activities.name: Dinner: Tonkatsu Maisen (Omotesandō)
activities.description: Widely considered Tokyo's best tonkatsu (breaded pork cutlet). The kurobuta (black pork) loin set is legendary. Located in a converted bathhouse in Omotesandō.

activities.name: Golden Gai Bar Crawl
activities.description: Six narrow alleys packed with over 200 tiny bars, each seating 5–10 people. Every bar has a theme — from jazz to horror to cats. This is where Tokyo's creative underbelly drinks. Most charge a small cover (¥500–1,000) plus drinks.

days.title: Bullet Train to Kyoto — Fushimi Inari & Gion
days.description: Shinkansen to Kyoto, hike the iconic orange torii gates of Fushimi Inari, then explore the geisha district and Kyoto's best food alley.

activities.name: Nozomi Bullet Train: Tokyo → Kyoto
activities.description: Board the Nozomi shinkansen from Tokyo Station to Kyoto Station. About 2 hours 15 minutes. Buy an ekiben (train bento) from the station for breakfast on the train.

activities.name: Fushimi Inari Shrine — The 10,000 Torii Gates
activities.description: Japan's most photographed shrine. Thousands of vermilion torii gates wind up the mountain behind the shrine. The full loop takes 2–3 hours, but you can turn around at any point. The first section (to the Yotsutsuji intersection) takes about 45 minutes and gives you the best photos.

activities.name: Vermillion Café or Local Udon
activities.description: Vermillion is a stylish café right near the shrine entrance — good coffee and light meals. Or walk to the Fushimi area for excellent kitsune udon (fried tofu udon, a local specialty since this is fox territory).

activities.name: Gion — Kyoto's Geisha District
activities.description: Walk through Japan's most atmospheric neighborhood. Wooden machiya townhouses, stone-paved streets, and if you're lucky, a glimpse of a maiko (apprentice geisha) heading to an evening engagement. Hanamikoji Street is the main avenue.

activities.name: Pontochō Alley
activities.description: A narrow alley running parallel to the Kamo River, packed with restaurants. Many have riverside balcony seating (kawadoko) in summer. October weather is perfect for this. Pick any place that looks good — the atmosphere is the star.

activities.name: Evening Walk: Ninenzaka & Sannenzaka Streets
activities.description: Even if Kiyomizu-dera isn't open for special night illumination, the streets leading up to it — Ninenzaka and Sannenzaka — are beautiful at night. Traditional shops, stone steps, and the pagoda lit up against the dark sky.

days.title: Bamboo Grove, Nintendo Museum & Chopstick Making
days.description: Kyoto's greatest hits plus your must-dos: morning in the bamboo forest, afternoon at the Nintendo Museum in Uji, and a hands-on chopstick making class.

activities.name: Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
activities.description: Towering bamboo stalks create a cathedral-like canopy overhead. It's magical — but ONLY if you arrive early. By 10 AM it's a sardine can. Get there at 7:30 AM for photos with almost no one around.

activities.name: Arashiyama Riverside & Tenryu-ji Temple
activities.description: Walk down to the iconic Togetsukyo Bridge spanning the Katsura River with mountains behind. Then visit Tenryu-ji, a UNESCO World Heritage Zen temple with one of Kyoto's finest gardens.

activities.name: Nintendo Museum
activities.description: Nintendo's first-ever museum, opened in 2024 in their original playing card factory in Uji (south of Kyoto). Interactive exhibits spanning from hanafuda cards to the Switch era. You can play oversized versions of classic Nintendo controllers. A must for any gamer.

activities.name: Matcha Everything in Uji
activities.description: Uji is THE matcha capital of Japan. The streets around Byodoin Temple are lined with matcha shops. Try matcha soba, matcha ice cream, matcha beer — everything is matcha here and it's all incredible.

activities.name: Chopstick Making Workshop
activities.description: Hand-carve your own pair of Japanese chopsticks using traditional woodworking techniques. You'll select your wood, shape them with a plane and knife, then lacquer or oil-finish them. A perfect Kyoto souvenir you actually made yourself.

activities.name: Nishiki Market Area Dinner
activities.description: Explore the evening scene around Nishiki Market (most stalls close by 5 PM, but surrounding restaurants stay open). Try Kyoto-style obanzai (tapas), or venture to one of the excellent yakitori joints in the area.

days.title: Himeji Castle Day Trip & Osaka Night
days.description: Day trip to Japan's most magnificent castle, then evening in Osaka — Japan's food capital — for street food and neon-soaked nightlife.

activities.name: Kyoto → Himeji by Shinkansen
activities.description: Quick bullet train ride west to Himeji, home to Japan's most spectacular castle. Only 45 minutes from Kyoto on the Hikari shinkansen.

activities.name: Himeji Castle (姫路城)
activities.description: Japan's largest and most visited castle, and a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The bright white exterior earned it the nickname 'White Heron Castle.' Unlike most Japanese castles, this one survived WWII intact — the wooden interiors are original. Climbing to the top floor rewards you with panoramic city views.

activities.name: Koko-en Garden
activities.description: Nine separate walled gardens right next to the castle, designed in traditional Edo-period style. The perfect wind-down after climbing the castle. The tea house overlooking the waterfall garden serves matcha and sweets.

activities.name: Himeji Lunch
activities.description: Try Himeji's local specialty: oden (particularly with ginger soy sauce, unique to this area) or pick up anago (conger eel) — the city's signature dish.

activities.name: Himeji → Osaka
activities.description: Hop on the Shinkansen or JR Special Rapid to Osaka. Shinkansen is 30 min, Special Rapid is about 60 min but much cheaper.

activities.name: Shinsekai — Osaka's Retro Playground
activities.description: A gloriously retro neighborhood that feels like 1960s Osaka. Neon signs, kushikatsu (deep-fried skewer) joints everywhere, and the iconic Tsutenkaku Tower. It's grimy, charismatic, and unapologetically Osaka.

activities.name: Dōtonbori — Osaka's Neon Food Street
activities.description: The most photographed street in Osaka. Giant mechanical crab, Glico running man sign, and hundreds of street food stalls. This is where you eat. A lot.

activities.name: Amerikamura & Bar Scene
activities.description: Osaka's nightlife is more relaxed and fun than Tokyo's. Amerikamura (American Village) is the young/hip district — vinyl shops, streetwear, dive bars. Or hit the standing bars (tachinomi) around Namba for cheap drinks with locals.

days.title: Osaka Deep Dive — Markets, Food & Culture
days.description: A full day discovering Osaka beyond the tourist trail. Morning at Japan's 'kitchen,' afternoon exploring the castle and creative neighborhoods, evening in the sky.

activities.name: Kuromon Market — Osaka's Kitchen
activities.description: A covered market that's been Osaka's pantry for over 190 years. Unlike Tsukiji (which has gotten very touristy), Kuromon still has a strong local vibe — especially early morning. Fresh sashimi, grilled seafood, and wagyu beef on sticks.

activities.name: Osaka Castle & Park
activities.description: Osaka's landmark castle surrounded by a massive moat and park. The castle itself is a concrete reconstruction (the interior is a museum), but the grounds and moat are spectacular. In October, you might catch early autumn colors.

activities.name: Nakazakichō — Osaka's Hidden Creative Quarter
activities.description: A neighborhood of renovated pre-war wooden houses turned into indie cafés, vintage shops, galleries, and bookstores. Zero tourists. This is where Osaka's creatives hang out. The polar opposite of Dōtonbori.

activities.name: Tenjinbashi-suji Shopping Street & Umeda Area
activities.description: Japan's longest covered shopping arcade at 2.6 km. Everything from daily goods to street food to vintage finds. Then head to the Umeda Sky Building for sunset views.

activities.name: Okonomiyaki — Osaka Style
activities.description: You cannot leave Osaka without eating okonomiyaki (savory pancake). Osaka-style means everything mixed together in batter (vs. Hiroshima's layered style). Watch it cook on the teppan grill in front of you.

activities.name: Optional: Spa World or Bar Hopping
activities.description: Spa World in Shinsekai is a massive multi-floor onsen complex with themed baths from around the world — great way to relax after two big days. Alternatively, explore Osaka's bar scene in Namba or Shinsaibashi.

days.title: Nara's Sacred Deer & Return to Kyoto
days.description: Morning with the bowing deer and ancient temples of Nara, then back to Kyoto for a quieter final evening in the old capital.

activities.name: Osaka → Nara
activities.description: Quick train ride from Osaka to Nara — Japan's first permanent capital. The entire park area is a UNESCO site, and over 1,000 friendly (and very hungry) deer roam freely.

activities.name: Todai-ji Temple & The Great Buddha
activities.description: Home to the world's largest bronze Buddha statue inside the world's largest wooden building. The scale is genuinely jaw-dropping — the building is so big your brain can't quite process it.

activities.name: Kasuga Taisha & The Lantern Path
activities.description: A Shinto shrine famous for its thousands of stone and bronze lanterns, many covered in moss. The approach through the ancient forest is mystical — deer rest among the lanterns under towering trees.

activities.name: Naramachi Old Town Lunch
activities.description: Walk south to Naramachi, the old merchant quarter. Narrow streets with restored machiya houses, many now housing restaurants, galleries, and shops.

activities.name: Nara → Kyoto
activities.description: Head back to Kyoto for your last evening in the old capital. Kintetsu line runs direct from Nara to Kyoto Station (35 min, ¥760).

activities.name: Kinkaku-ji — The Golden Pavilion
activities.description: Kyoto's most iconic image: a Zen temple covered in gold leaf, reflected perfectly in a mirror pond. Smaller than you expect but more stunning in person than any photo can capture.

activities.name: Kyoto Farewell Dinner
activities.description: One last Kyoto meal before heading to Hakone tomorrow. Treat yourselves to something special — perhaps a counter-seat kappo (Japanese haute cuisine served casually at the counter) or your favorites from the trip so far.

days.title: Hakone — Private Onsen & Mountain Escape
days.description: Leave the cities behind for Hakone's volcanic hot springs, mountain railways, and breathtaking lake views. Tonight: your private onsen ryokan — the highlight of the trip.

activities.name: Shinkansen to Odawara, then Hakone
activities.description: Take the shinkansen from Kyoto to Odawara (about 2 hours on Hikari), then switch to the Hakone Tozan Railway into the mountains. The transition from city to mountain is magical.

activities.name: Hakone Tozan Railway → Gōra → Cable Car → Ropeway
activities.description: The classic Hakone sightseeing loop. A switchback mountain railway climbs to Gōra, then a cable car and aerial ropeway take you over volcanic valleys with views of Mount Fuji (weather permitting).

activities.name: Ōwakudani — Great Boiling Valley
activities.description: An active volcanic zone with sulfurous steam vents, bubbling pools, and the smell of rotten eggs. The star attraction: kuro-tamago (black eggs) boiled in the volcanic hot springs — eating one supposedly adds 7 years to your life.

activities.name: Hakone Sightseeing Cruise on Lake Ashi
activities.description: Take the ropeway down to Togendai and board a pirate ship (yes, literally a pirate-themed cruise ship) across Lake Ashi. On clear days, Mt. Fuji towers over the lake and the red torii gate of Hakone Shrine emerges from the forest on the shore.

activities.name: Hakone Shrine & Lake Torii
activities.description: A Shinto shrine set in ancient cedar forest on the shore of Lake Ashi. The red torii gate standing in the lake is one of Japan's most photographed spots. Peaceful and atmospheric.

activities.name: Private Onsen Ryokan — Your Hakone Retreat
activities.description: This is the moment. Check into your ryokan with a private onsen (kashikiri or room-attached). Change into your yukata (cotton robe), sink into the steaming outdoor bath surrounded by mountain forest, and let the volcanic mineral waters dissolve two weeks of travel.

activities.time: 🍽️ 7:00 PM — Kaiseki Dinner at the Ryokan
activities.name: Kaiseki Dinner
activities.description: A multi-course Japanese dinner served at your ryokan — typically 8–12 courses showcasing seasonal ingredients, local fish, wagyu, and delicate preparations you won't find anywhere else. October means matsutake mushroom, sweet potato, chestnuts, and autumn fruits.

activities.name: Evening Private Onsen Soak
activities.description: After dinner, slip back into the private outdoor bath under the stars. Mountain silence, steam rising, stars overhead. This is what you came for.

days.title: Hakone Morning & Return to Tokyo — Park Hyatt
days.description: One last onsen soak at dawn, then return to Tokyo in style. Check into the Park Hyatt for your final two nights — Lost in Translation vibes, 52nd-floor views.

activities.name: Morning Onsen Soak
activities.description: Wake up early for a dawn soak. The morning light filtering through the mountain mist into the outdoor bath is otherworldly. Most ryokan baths are open from 5 or 6 AM.

activities.name: Traditional Japanese Breakfast
activities.description: Ryokan breakfast is a full spread: grilled fish (usually salmon or mackerel), rice, miso soup, pickled vegetables, tofu, natto (fermented soybeans, try it!), tamagoyaki (rolled omelette), and green tea.

activities.time: 🚃 10:00 AM — Check Out & Head to Tokyo
activities.name: Hakone → Tokyo (Shinjuku)
activities.description: Check out of your ryokan and head back to Tokyo. Take the Romancecar from Hakone-Yumoto directly to Shinjuku — it's a scenic express with big windows and reserved seats. About 85 minutes.

activities.time: 🏨 12:30 PM — Check Into Park Hyatt Tokyo
activities.name: Park Hyatt Tokyo
activities.description: Your home for the final two nights. This is THE Lost in Translation hotel — where Bill Murray drank whisky at the New York Bar on the 52nd floor. The views over Shinjuku from the pool and bar are legendary. The lobby is on the 41st floor. Welcome to luxury.

activities.name: Fuunji Tsukemen
activities.description: Widely considered Tokyo's best tsukemen (dipping ramen). The ultra-rich fish-pork broth is served in a separate bowl — dip the thick, chewy noodles in and slurp. There's always a line, but it moves fast.

activities.name: Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden
activities.description: One of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, combining Japanese, English, and French garden styles. In mid-October, you'll catch the beginning of autumn colors. A peaceful escape from the Shinjuku chaos just outside the walls.

activities.name: Harajuku & Omotesandō
activities.description: Harajuku is Tokyo's street fashion and youth culture epicenter. Takeshita Street is sensory overload — crepe stands, costume shops, and teen fashion. Omotesandō (the boulevard above) is the upscale counterpoint: designer boutiques in striking architecture.

activities.time: 🍸 7:30 PM — New York Bar at Park Hyatt
activities.name: New York Bar — Lost in Translation
activities.description: The bar where Scarlett Johansson and Bill Murray shared those late-night moments. Live jazz every night, floor-to-ceiling windows, and the most cinematic view in Tokyo. Dress smart casual. Get here by 7:30 PM to avoid the cover charge (starts at 8 PM on music nights).

days.title: Last Day — Souvenir Run, Last Meals & Departure
days.description: Make every hour count before your 5:20 PM NRT departure. Morning shopping, a farewell lunch, then head to the airport with memories (and snacks) to last a lifetime.

activities.name: Breakfast at Girandole or New York Grill
activities.description: The Park Hyatt's breakfast is excellent — Girandole (41F) serves a lavish buffet with both Western and Japanese options, while the New York Grill (52F) offers à la carte breakfast with those views. Treat yourselves on the last morning.

activities.name: Souvenir & Gift Shopping
activities.description: Dedicated time for the souvenir run. Tokyo Station and Ginza have the best curated gift shopping in one area.

activities.name: Final Tokyo Meal
activities.description: One last great meal before the airport. Make it count — sushi, ramen, whatever you've been craving one more time.

activities.name: Shinjuku → Narita Airport
activities.description: You need to be at NRT by 3:00 PM for your 5:20 PM flight (international flights: arrive 2+ hours early). From Shinjuku, the Narita Express takes about 80 minutes.

activities.name: Last Moments in Japan
activities.description: Arrive at NRT with time to spare. Clear security, do last-minute duty-free shopping (Japanese whisky, KitKats, skincare), and grab one final onigiri from a convenience store.
